papers.title: Unified definition of integrated diagnostics: a position statement of the EFLM.
papers.abstract: Integrated diagnostics is an emerging multidisciplinary model of care that integrates traditionally siloed domains, including pathology, radiology, genomics, and laboratory medicine, into a coordinated framework designed to improve diagnostic accuracy, treatment selection, and clinical outcomes. In this position statement, the EFLM Integrated Diagnostics Committee proposes a concise and operational definition of integrated diagnostics and outlines the relevance for healthcare systems. Integrated diagnostics has the potential to advance precision medicine through improved data integration, more coordinated interpretation, and enhanced clinical decision-making. Drawing on multidisciplinary expert consensus, we recommend adoption of a standardized conceptual framework to support research, clinical implementation, interoperability, and policy development across healthcare systems with implementation adapted to local needs, scale, and digital maturity.
authors: European Federation of Clinical Chemistry and Laboratory Medicine (EFLM) Committee: Integrative Diagnostics

papers.title: Type III effector repertoires as a window into Pseudomonas syringae pv . actinidiae evolution and Actinidia defense responses.
papers.abstract: Kiwifruit bacterial canker, caused by Pseudomonas syringae pv. actinidiae (Psa), represents a complex disease system in which closely related bacterial populations differ in host association, pathogenicity, genomic composition, and geographic distribution as evidenced by pandemic spread of biovar 3 after 2008. Closely related Psa lineages differ in host association, virulence, and distribution, yet these differences arise largely outside the conserved core genome. Mobile genetic elements remodel accessory regions, and acquisition, loss, and redundancy of type III effectors shape whether a lineage colonizes or is restricted by a given Actinidia genotype. Virulence is therefore a host-dependent property, not a fixed lineage rank. On the host side, genome assemblies, QTL mapping, and infection transcriptomics indicate that resistance reflects the timing and persistence of immune signalling rather than receptor presence alone, although few candidate receptors have been validated in planta. Durable resistance is most likely to derive from recognition of non-redundant effector functions and from immune hubs, such as RIN4, that multiple effectors target. Integrating pathogen population genomics, effector biology, and host immune genetics is the route to predicting which lineages will emerge next.

papers.title: Respiratory pathogens across rural populations: general practice patients with community-acquired pneumonia, residents, and goat farmers.
papers.abstract: Residents living near goat farms (< 2000 m) in the Netherlands have consistently shown an elevated risk of pneumonia, yet the pathogens underlying this association remain unknown. This study assessed the presence of 33 respiratory pathogens, including bacteria, viruses, and fungi, across rural populations with different goat farm exposures. This cross-sectional study included general practitioner (GP)-diagnosed pneumonia patients (PP; n = 108), non-farming rural residents without pneumonia (NFR; n = 200), and goat farm workers (GFW; n = 91). Oropharyngeal and nasopharyngeal swabs were collected and analyzed by a multiplex and two additional PCR test targeting in total 12 bacteria, 20 viruses and 1 fungus. Between-group differences in detection were assessed by Fisher's exact tests. Logistic regression analyses were performed to assess associations between pathogen detection and residential proximity to goat farming and other covariates. Presence of any of the examined pathogens was highest in the PP group (94.5%), followed by GFW (88.8%), and NFR (70%). The most frequently detected pathogens overall were Haemophilus influenzae, Staphylococcus aureus, Streptococcus pneumoniae, Moraxella catarrhalis, and rhinovirus. Of these, M. catarrhalis and S. pneumoniae were significantly more often detected in PP, whereas Salmonella spp. and S. aureus were more frequently detected in GFW. Eight pathogens, including Coxiella burnetii, were not detected. Age, season of sampling, smoking and other covariates were significantly associated with certain bacteria and viruses. However, no associations were identified between residential proximity to goat farming and detection of specific pathogens in NFR and PP. Respiratory pathogens were detected in nearly all PP, while substantial proportions of positives were also observed in GFW and NFR, likely reflecting (transient) colonization rather than active infection. Detection of the examined pathogens was not associated with residential proximity to goat farms, suggesting that these pathogens do not explain the observed increased pneumonia risk among nearby non-farming residents. As a substantial proportion of the Dutch population (~ 7%) lives within 2,000 m of a commercial goat farm, and goat farming is expanding globally, further research efforts, including microbiologic diagnostics and surveillance, are needed to elucidate the mechanisms underlying the increased pneumonia risk among nearby residents.
authors: Joke W B van der Giessen

papers.title: PPT1-mediated GABA A Rα1 depalmitoylation maintains inhibitory synaptic homeostasis and cognition.
papers.abstract: GABA A receptors (GABA A Rs), essential for inhibitory neurotransmission, are palmitoylated proteins and their depalmitoylation is catalyzed by palmitoyl-protein thioesterase 1 (PPT1). By generating Gabra1 em1 knock-in mice carrying mutations that disrupt the interaction between GABA A Rα1 and PPT1, we found that the mutant mice exhibited impaired learning and memory, whereas the underlying cellular mechanisms remained largely unclear. Molecular analyses showed that heterozygous (HET) Gabra1 em1 mice (Gabra1 em1 HET) displayed normal GABA A Rα1 protein expression but persistent hyperpalmitoylation of GABA A Rα1. Electrophysiological recordings demonstrated the decreased neuronal excitability, enhanced inhibitory synaptic transmission and impaired hippocampal long-term potentiation (LTP). Behavioral analyses further revealed deficits in learning, memory and social behavior. The homozygous (HOMO) Gabra1 em1 mice (Gabra1 em1 HOMO) exhibited a marked reduction in GABA A Rα1 protein expression, accompanied by enhanced neuronal excitability and excitatory synaptic transmission, but impaired LTP and learning and memory along with a shorten life span. Collectively, these findings indicate that Gabra1 em1 HET mice represent a valuable model for investigating the physiological and pathological roles of protein palmitoylation, as aberrant GABA A Rα1 palmitoylation disrupts neuronal excitability, synaptic plasticity, and cognitive function without altering receptor expression. In contrast, the phenotypes observed in Gabra1 em1 HOMO mice are primarily attributable to the marked reduction in GABA A Rα1 protein expression, which consequently impairs synaptic plasticity and learning and memory. These findings provide new mechanistic insights into the role of protein palmitoylation in neurological disorders and offer a theoretical foundation for the development of precision therapeutic strategies targeting palmitoylation homeostasis.

papers.title: Precision medicine approaches in diabetic cardiomyopathy: from molecular mechanisms to personalized therapeutic strategies.
papers.abstract: Diabetic cardiomyopathy (DCM) is a distinct myocardial disease defined by the existence of abnormal myocardial structure and performance in diabetes mellitus patients without hypertension and coronary artery disease. DCM has been identified as a major cause of heart failure, hospitalisation and cardiovascular mortality with increasing global burden of diabetes. However, there is a large interindividual variation in disease susceptibility, disease progression and response to therapy, highlighting the limitations of conventional management strategies that are applied uniformly. Precision medicine provides a transformational approach through the integration of genomic, molecular, imaging, clinical and lifestyle data to allow for personalized risk assessment, early diagnosis, prognostication and treatment. This review presents the recent advances in the field of precision medicine for DCM with a focus on the molecular pathological mechanisms including metabolic disorders, oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, inflammation, fibrosis and microvascular injury. We discuss the relevance of genomics, pharmacogenomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics, lipidomics and epigenomics in the context of disease heterogeneity and identification of novel therapeutic targets. Emerging biomarkers including circulating microRNAs, non-coding RNAs, inflammatory mediators, fibrosis-related markers and extracellular vesicles are discussed for their potential in personal diagnosis and prognosis. We also consider the increasing role of advanced cardiac imaging, digital phenotyping, wearable technologies, artificial intelligence, and machine learning in enhancing early detection and clinical decision-making. In this review, the therapeutic advances, including sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors, glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists, anti-fibrotic therapies, mitochondrial-targeted interventions, regenerative medicine, gene therapy, and RNA-based therapeutics, are discussed, with a focus on the precision medicine approach. Finally, we present current challenges in data integration, clinical validation, cost-effectiveness, and ethical issues, and highlight future directions in digital twins, multi-omics integration, and AI-driven personalized cardiology. The combination of these technologies has the potential to revolutionize the prevention and management of diabetic cardiomyopathy and improve cardiovascular outcomes in patients with diabetes.

papers.title: A dual-mode colorimetric and fluorescent sensing platform based on MnO 2 nanosheets for sensitive detection of Escherichia coli.
papers.abstract: The timely and accurate identification of Escherichia coli (E. coli) plays a pivotal role in controlling foodborne infections and safeguarding public well-being. We designed a dual-mode sensing strategy based on manganese dioxide nanosheets (MnO 2 NS) to detect E. coli through colorimetric and fluorescent methods. E. coli could catalyze the conversion of p-benzoquinone (BQ) to hydroquinone (HQ) via an enzymatic reaction. Subsequently, HQ reduced MnO 2 NS to Mn 2+ , leading to a decrease in the oxidase-like activity of MnO 2 NS towards 3, 3', 5, 5'-tetramethylbenzidine (TMB) and amplex red (AR). As a result, based on the changes in absorbance at 652 nm and fluorescence intensity at 582 nm, E. coli was detected in the ranges 1.0 × 10 1 - 1.0 × 10 6 CFU/mL and 1.0 × 10 1 - 1.0 × 10 8 CFU/mL, respectively. The limits of detection were 1 CFU/mL and 5 CFU/mL, respectively. Furthermore, this MnO 2 NS-based colorimetric and fluorescent sensing strategy enabled accurate detection of E. coli in spiked milk samples. In summary, the developed strategy demonstrates significant potential for practical applications in foodborne pathogen detection.

papers.title: From laboratory quantification to rapid on-site testing: Screening of high-affinity monoclonal antibody pairs targeting the RSV F protein and analytical evaluation across multiple assay platforms.
papers.abstract: Monoclonal antibodies against respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) F protein are key reagents for antigen-based diagnosis, yet antibody pairs compatible with multiple assay formats remain limited. In this study, BALB/c mice were immunized with recombinant postfusion RSV F protein, yielding six hybridoma cell lines secreting anti-RSV F monoclonal antibodies. The antibodies were characterized by indirect ELISA, Western blotting, and surface plasmon resonance, and the optimal sandwich pair was selected by cross-pairing ELISA. The mAb-14/mAb-26 pair showed high affinity and the best pairing performance and was used to establish double-antibody sandwich ELISA (DAS-ELISA), magnetic microparticle-based chemiluminescent immunoassay, and Au@Pt nanoparticle-based lateral flow immunoassay (Au@Pt-LFIA). The limits of detection were 0.25, 0.04, and 0.78 ng/mL, respectively. Au@Pt-LFIA achieved an approximately fourfold lower visual detection limit than conventional colloidal gold immunochromatography without additional signal-amplification steps. None of the three methods showed detectable cross-reactivity with the seven tested heterologous respiratory pathogen antigens. In preliminary clinical sample testing, the positive percent agreements of DAS-ELISA, chemiluminescent immunoassay, and Au@Pt-LFIA were 90.0%, 93.3%, and 83.3%, respectively, and the negative percent agreements were 100.0% for all methods. These results support mAb-14/mAb-26 as a versatile antibody pair for RSV antigen detection across complementary laboratory and on-site assay platforms.

papers.title: Establishment and preliminary application of the Mo RPA-CRISPR/Cas12a rapid detection method.
papers.abstract: Mycoplasma ovipneumoniae ( Mo ) is a common pathogen prevalent worldwide that causes pneumonia and leads to significant economic losses in sheep farming. Early testing of nasal swabs from diseased sheep in Xinjiang yielded a 51.5% positivity rate, indicating severe infection within the sheep population. Existing detection methods are time-consuming and rely on large-scale equipment, making them unsuitable for frontline clinical testing. Rapid, accurate, and on-site pathogen detection is essential for the early prevention and control of infectious diseases. Conventional nucleic acid detection methods are limited by long reaction duration, sophisticated instruments, and strict operating requirements, which restrict their application in grassroots rapid diagnosis scenarios. Herein, we established a combined Mo -RPA integrated CRISPR/Cas12a detection assay, which realized constant-temperature nucleic acid detection without large-scale laboratory equipment. The entire detection workflow was completed within 30 min under a constant temperature of 37°C. The optimized assay achieved a limit of detection of 10° copies/μL, with 100% analytical specificity against non-target pathogen strains. In clinical sample verification, the detection consistency between the established method and standard real-time PCR assay reached 100%. The established constant-temperature detection system integrates rapid nucleic acid amplification and CRISPR fluorescent signal output and provides a quantifiable on-site detection scheme for grassroots epidemic surveillance. In this study, we demonstrated a novel RPA-CRISPR-Cas12a-based diagnostic method for Mycoplasma ovipneumoniae ( Mo ) infection with high sensitivity and specificity. The detection rate reached 51.5% (85/165). Subsequently, an RPA-CRISPR/Cas12a rapid test targeting the 16S rRNA gene of Mo was developed, achieving a detection time of 30 min, 100% specificity, and a sensitivity of 100 copies/μL-10⁶ times more sensitive than PCR. During preliminary application, the RPA-CRISPR/Cas12a method detected Mo in 84/102 samples (82.35%), representing 1.7 times the detection rate of PCR. Consequently, RPA-Cas12a testing has demonstrated significant potential for routine Mo screening and offers high accessibility for population screening or molecular diagnostics in resource-limited settings.

papers.title: Phloretin Ameliorates Rheumatoid Arthritis by Suppressing HIF-1α-Dependent Angiogenesis and Modulating of the Autophagy-Apoptosis Balance.
papers.abstract: Phloretin (PHL) is an effective monomer component of Phellodendri Chinensis Cortex, Spica Prunellae, and fleshy fruits and exerts therapeutic effects on rheumatoid arthritis (RA). However, the underlying mechanism is yet to be elucidated. Following PHL treatment, therapeutic benefits were evaluated in a collagen-induced arthritis (CIA) rat model using arthritic markers and joint pathology. Network pharmacology, transcriptomics, Western blotting, IHC, molecular docking, Biacore, and cellular thermal shift assay were employed. PHL administration considerably reduced joint swelling, synovial hyperplasia, and bone erosion. Integrated network pharmacology and transcriptomic analyses identified the hypoxia-inducible factor-1 alpha (HIF-1α) axis as a critical target. In vitro experiments indicated that PHL effectively inhibited TNF-α-induced fibroblast-like synoviocyte (FLS) proliferation, migration, invasion, and glycolytic reprogramming, promoted apoptosis, and suppressed excessive autophagy. Furthermore, in a coculture system, PHL substantially attenuated FLS-induced tube formation in human umbilical vein endothelial cells. Furthermore, PHL demonstrated high affinity for HIF-1α and accelerated the degradation of HIF-1α protein. Importantly, HIF-1α overexpression reversed PHL's inhibitory effect. RA severity was alleviated in Hif1a +/- mice, validating HIF-1α's pathogenic role in disease progression. PHL exerts anti-RA effects by targeting HIF-1α to modulate glycolysis and the autophagy-apoptosis balance in FLS, thereby inhibiting synovial angiogenesis. These findings provide a strong foundation for developing and applying PHL as a potential therapeutic agent for RA.

papers.title: Diagnostic accuracy and clinical considerations of metagenomic next-generation sequencing in prosthetic joint infection: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
papers.abstract: Metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) has emerged as a promising complementary method for pathogen detection in prosthetic joint infection (PJI). This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the diagnostic accuracy of mNGS and conventional microbiological culture. A systematic review and bivariate diagnostic accuracy meta-analysis were conducted in accordance with the PRISMA-DTA guidelines. PubMed, Ovid MEDLINE, Embase, WoS and the CNKI database were searched. Eligible studies evaluated shotgun mNGS in suspected or confirmed PJI, used a recognized reference standard for diagnosis, and reported sufficient data to construct 2 × 2 contingency tables for mNGS and conventional culture. Pooled sensitivity and specificity were estimated using a bivariate random-effects Reitsma model. Fourteen studies comprising 1,579 cases were included, of which 982 were classified as PJI and 597 as non-PJI. When pooled separately, mNGS had a sensitivity of 84.3% (95% CI 77.3-89.4%) and specificity of 91.5% (95% CI 88.4-93.9%), compared with 66.0% (95% CI 60.1-71.4%) and 95.6% (95% CI 92.8-97.4%), respectively, for conventional culture. The area under the summary receiver operating characteristic (SROC) curve was 0.941 for mNGS and 0.930 for culture. Sensitivity analyses did not change the overall findings. When analysed separately, mNGS demonstrated higher pooled sensitivity than conventional culture. Overall diagnostic performance assessed by SROC was comparable between the two methods. These findings suggest that mNGS may provide complementary microbiological information. Nevertheless, microorganisms detected exclusively by mNGS should be interpreted cautiously and in conjunction with other clinical and laboratory findings.

papers.title: Hospital Water Safety and Nontuberculous Mycobacteria Risk: A National Evaluation of Organisational Readiness Across NHS Hospitals.
papers.abstract: Following a Prevention of Future Deaths report highlighting risks from Mycobacterium abscessus in hospital water systems, NHS Estates Technical Bulletin (NETB) 2024/3 introduced updated measures to reduce risks from waterborne pathogens, including nontuberculous mycobacteria (NTM). This study described organisational responses and reported surveillance, design practices and water safety controls across NHS providers in England following publication of the bulletin. A Freedom of Information Survey was sent to all NHS England organisations (n = 180). Questions explored awareness of NETB 2024/3; high-risk patient groups; water safety governance; NTM testing; control/remediation measures; and design activities. Structured data were collated, and free-text responses thematically analysed. The response rate was 90% (n=162). Awareness of NETB 2024/3 guidance was high (n=145, 90%), and almost all organisations had Water Safety Groups (99%). 71% reported caring for high-risk patient groups (n=115). Environmental NTM testing was undertaken by 14 Trusts (9%), six of these (42.9%) reported NTM detection, most often heater-cooler units and theatres. 13% (n=21) had Water Safety Plans specifically defining NTM risk mitigation. Testing strategies varied, from reactive sampling to scheduled programmes. Control measures for waterborne pathogens generally included temperature management (98%) and outlet descaling (94%); 70% (n=113) had undertaken design modifications in high-risk areas. Design and control measures for waterborne pathogens varied considerably between organisations. Common themes included pipework reconfiguration and reduced use of tap water for patient care. Approaches to NTM testing and management were heterogeneous. Greater consensus on when environmental NTM testing informs management, and how results should guide action, could support organisational decision-making.

papers.title: Applications of Artificial Intelligence in Parasitology: A holistic perspective from diagnosis to therapeutics.
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly being investigated to address challenges in parasite detection, disease surveillance, and therapeutic development. This narrative review examines current and emerging AI applications in parasitology across diagnostics, drug discovery, genomics, epidemiology, education, and public health decision-making, with particular emphasis on diagnostic applications. Machine learning and deep learning methods support automated parasite detection, classification, and quantification in microscopic images, alongside medical image analysis and arthropod identification. Applications are discussed for malaria, leishmaniasis, schistosomiasis, cystic echinococcosis, soil-transmitted helminth infections, and intestinal protozoal infections. Beyond diagnosis, AI-assisted approaches support compound screening, drug repurposing, toxicity prediction, and prioritization of potential therapeutic targets. Genomic and transcriptomic analyses also offer opportunities to investigate parasite biology and predict drug resistance. Surveillance models may inform outbreak forecasting and targeted control, although their operational value requires evaluation in the intended settings. Educational applications remain emerging, and the benefits of digital learning should be distinguished from those attributable specifically to AI. Across these domains, performance on curated datasets does not establish clinical utility or generalizability. Major barriers include limited representative datasets, insufficient external and prospective validation, infrastructure constraints, and concerns regarding privacy, bias, and accountability. Future progress requires reproducible evaluation, experimental validation of therapeutic candidates, and assessment of clinical and public health benefits. AI is therefore best positioned as a complementary tool that supports parasitological expertise, with responsible implementation guided by transparency, equitable access, and human oversight.

papers.title: Neurodegeneration in sub-Saharan Africa: Intersections of biological ageing, genomic diversity and the lifetime exposome.
papers.abstract: Neurodegenerative diseases are emerging as an important consequence of population ageing in sub-Saharan Africa (SSA), but their scientific relevance extends beyond a projected rise in case numbers. SSA combines exceptional human genomic diversity with marked heterogeneity in vascular and metabolic risk, infection, nutrition, occupational exposures, air pollution, and access to health care. This combination creates an underused setting in which to study why biological ageing produces neurodegeneration in some individuals but relative resilience in others. This review critically synthesises evidence on Alzheimer's disease and related dementias, Parkinson's disease, amyotrophic lateral sclerosis/frontotemporal degeneration, Huntington's disease and related disorders, focusing on the intersection between hallmarks of ageing, disease-specific proteinopathies, ancestry and the lifetime exposome. Age-associated loss of proteostasis, mitochondrial dysfunction, impaired autophagy, chronic inflammation, neurovascular injury and genomic/epigenomic instability provide a mechanistic scaffold on which genetic susceptibility and cumulative exposures may act. Yet African evidence remains dominated by cross-sectional clinical phenotyping; neuropathology, longitudinal biomarkers, multi-omics and measured environmental exposures remain sparse. Recent African-ancestry Parkinson's disease genomics and emerging plasma biomarker studies demonstrate that ancestry-inclusive molecular neuroscience is feasible and can generate findings not predictable from European-ancestry datasets. The next phase should therefore move beyond documenting underdiagnosis toward longitudinal, biologically anchored cohorts that integrate phenotype, genomics, blood biomarkers, neuroimaging, exposomics, digital measures and health-system outcomes. This review proposes a research framework centred on biological ageing, gene-environment interaction and resilience. Such work would improve the validity of prevention, diagnosis and therapeutic translation in African populations while contributing globally to a more complete biology of neurodegenerative ageing.

papers.title: Host life history traits as drivers of viral infection in European bats.
papers.abstract: Bats are recognized as natural reservoirs of a wide range of viruses. Understanding the factors that determine patterns of viral occurrence in reservoir species, particularly viral richness and viral detection frequency, is essential for explaining host-pathogen dynamics and anticipating public health risks. In this study, we evaluated the influence of life-history traits on viral frequency (defined as the proportion of positive detections across studies) in European bats for six important viral groups (Adenoviridae, Herpesviridae, Papillomaviridae, Filoviridae, Coronaviridae, and the genus Lyssavirus within Rhabdoviridae) through a systematic review, identifying 7,037 publications, of which 155 met the inclusion criteria. These studies focused primarily on three species: Cnephaeus serotinus, Myotis daubentonii, and Pipistrellus pipistrellus. We detected a phylogenetic signal in viral frequency only for the family Adenoviridae and genus Betacoronavirus, suggesting that these viral groups have a particular evolutionary affinity with their hosts. Viral frequency was associated with bats' environmental breadth and body size, although these relationships were not consistent across all viral groups. Instead, each viral group was associated with a distinct set of host life-history traits, reflecting -most probably- differences in their ecology and evolutionary history. Overall, our findings demonstrate that the ecological drivers of viral frequency are virus-specific rather than universal.

papers.title: Automated standardization of legacy biomedical metadata using an ontology-constrained LLM agent.
papers.abstract: Descriptive scientific metadata in public repositories are often incomplete and inconsistent with community standards and ontologies, limiting data FAIRness. Large language models (LLMs) offer a promising approach to automatically standardizing such metadata when the LLM is provided with knowledge of the relevant standards in machine-actionable form (e.g., as metadata templates from systems such as the CEDAR Workbench). Entry of metadata standards through prompt engineering offers only fixed snapshots of the relevant standards, however, and it relies on an LLM's pretrained knowledge to interpret and satisfy constraints related to the standard. We evaluate whether giving an LLM access to metadata specifications and authoritative terminology at runtime improves automated metadata standardization. We present ARMS, a tool-using LLM agent that retrieves complete CEDAR metadata templates and that queries authoritative biomedical terminology services dynamically at execution time. We compared ARMS with a prompt-engineering approach on 839 legacy metadata records describing experiment datasets from the Human BioMolecular Atlas Program (HuBMAP) with expert-standardized records serving as the reference standard. Across the corpus, ARMS outperformed the prompt-engineering approach in converting legacy metadata to standards-compliant form, increasing precision from 0.56 to 0.93 and recall from 0.51 to 0.85, with improvements across all field categories and assay types. The largest gains occurred for ontology-constrained fields, where precision increased from 0.36 to 0.92. Our findings show that access to appropriate metadata standards can substantially improve LLM-based standardization of legacy metadata. ARMS improves metadata standardization by giving LLMs runtime access to the authoritative resources that define valid metadata. Representation of metadata standards in machine-actionable form enhances the task of rectifying legacy metadata using LLM technology, especially when those standards can be queried dynamically.

papers.title: erm(46) copy number determines macrolide resistance in Rhodococcus equi.
papers.abstract: To develop a multiplex real-time PCR assay for simultaneous detection of Rhodococcus equi (choE), virulence (vapA), and macrolide-resistance determinants (erm[46], erm[51]), and evaluate their clinical and temporal trends. Clinical R equi isolates (n = 229) obtained from the Hagyard Equine Medical Institute laboratory were collected sequentially over a 3-year surveillance period (2021 to 2023) from 14 states and underwent broth microdilution susceptibility testing. A cohort of 214 isolates with high-quality DNA was characterized using quantitative PCR. Geographic distribution, seasonal trends, and genotypic-phenotypic concordance were evaluated. The multiplex PCR assay demonstrated 100% analytical specificity. The virulence gene vapA was present in 94.4% (202 of 214) of isolates. The macrolide resistance determinant erm(46) was highly prevalent at 62.6% (134 of 214), showing a significant seasonal increase during July to December periods at 76.6% (vs 58.2% in January to June). Crucially, erm(51) was detected in a single isolate (0.5%), representing its first recorded clinical identification in R equi. Unstratified genotypic-phenotypic agreement for macrolides was fair (κ = 0.22 to 0.25). However, stratification by genomic copy number revealed near-perfect concordance (κ ≥ 0.97) exclusively among isolates harboring > 50,000 target copies. Alternative agents (gentamicin, ceftiofur, minocycline, doxycycline) maintained 97% to 100% susceptibility, regardless of erm(46) status. While erm(46) is widely distributed across R equi-endemic farms, actual phenotypic resistance expression is strongly copy-number dependent. The clinical emergence of erm(51) expands the known resistome of this pathogen. Incorporating quantitative molecular screening into routine R equi diagnostics provides crucial real-time therapeutic guidance, supporting precision medicine and targeted antimicrobial stewardship on endemic equine farms.

papers.title: Functional stratification of YWHAZ variants explains distinct neurodevelopmental disorders.
papers.abstract: The application of clinical genomics in personalized medical practice increasingly reveals that variants from single loci can lead to phenotypic heterogeneity. This necessitates functional characterization and classification of serial variants to correlate their associated clinical features and molecular properties. Recently, a few putative pathogenic variants in YWHAZ, encoding the 14-3-3ζ protein, have been implicated in clinically variable isolated and syndromic neurodevelopmental phenotypes, based on a few reported affected individuals, but the molecular basis of this heterogeneity has remained unclear. Here, we assembled a large cohort of individuals harboring de novo YWHAZ variants and categorized their clinical stratification into distinct neurodevelopmental conditions, including a typical presentation of cardiofaciocutaneous syndrome and a developmental and epileptic encephalopathy with sleep disorders. By integrating structural analyses, molecular dynamics simulations, in vitro biochemical and cell-based signaling studies, unbiased proteomics analysis, and in vivo phenotypic assays, we define distinct functional classes of pathogenic YWHAZ variants and establish robust genotype-phenotype correlations. We show that disease-associated YWHAZ variants differentially perturb 14-3-3ζ function by variably affecting protein abundance and binding to interacting partners, including the BRAF and RAF1 kinases. Notably, the recurrent p.Ser230Trp (c.689C>G) variant uniquely underlying cardiofaciocutaneous syndrome specifically enhances MAPK signaling, whereas other variants do not significantly impact signal flow through the cascade under the used experimental conditions. Our data establish a mechanistic framework linking allelic variation in YWHAZ to phenotypic heterogeneity.

papers.title: Comparative Proteomics of Extracellular Vesicles of Two Species of Mucorales Reveals Species-Specific Cargo.
papers.abstract: Rhizopus arrhizus is one of the most common etiological agents of mucormycosis worldwide, whereas Mucor irregularis has been reported with a relatively high frequency in China, exhibiting clear regional characteristics. However, the molecular basis underlying their differential host responses remains incompletely understood. Fungal extracellular vesicles (EVs) play diverse biological roles across fungal species and have emerged as important carriers of bioactive cargos that modulate host-pathogen interactions. In this study, we compared features of EVs derived from R. arrhizus and M. irregularis and evaluated their immunomodulatory effects. EVs were isolated from PBS suspensions collected from fungal cultures via differential ultracentrifugation, followed by physical and proteomic characterization. Quantitative proteomics via DIA (data independent acquisition) identified 246 EV-associated proteins showing species-specific detection or quantitative abundance differences between the two species. In the murine footpad infection model, R. arrhizus induced more severe local lesions than M. irregularis, whereas EVs from M. irregularis elicited substantially higher pro-inflammatory cytokine expression in RAW 264.7 macrophages in vitro. Collectively, our results demonstrate marked divergence between R. arrhizus and M. irregularis in EV size, protein composition, and macrophage responses, providing a comparative resource for further investigation of EV-associated factors in Mucorales-host interactions.

papers.title: Perspectives on ethics, equity, and genomic data governance in Kenya: insights from the 2026 human genetics and genomics society of Kenya symposium.
papers.abstract: Kenya is at a transitional point in advancing human genomics research and its applications particularly for non-communicable diseases. While there are foundational legal and institutional infrastructures in place there are still significant governance gaps that exist that need to be addressed before large-scale human genomic research, and genomic medicine can be implemented in a responsible manner. This is a report on the perspectives gathered from symposium participants attending the 2nd Human Genetics and Genomics Society of Kenya (HGGSK) symposium, held during 16th KEMRI Annual Scientific and Health Conference. It draws on narrative/ descriptive synthesis of expert speaker presentations and a structured survey completed by symposium attendees to provide insight on ethics, equity, and genomic data governance in Kenya. Most respondents 13/23 (57%) perceived that Kenya is not yet adequately prepared for the implementation of large-scale human genomics research. The primary concerns were the need for stronger genetic privacy protections, robust informed consent processes, and a national genomics policy framework. A large majority of participants 19/23 (83%) emphasized the need to strengthen genetic privacy protection, while 12/23 (52%) preferred study-specific consent over broad consent for the future use of genomic data. Overall, participants identified the development of a national human genomics policy framework as the most urgent priority to support the responsible advancement of human genomics research and its clinical implementation in Kenya. Kenya has foundational structures for human genomics research but there is a need to develop governance frameworks that will guide responsible scaling.

papers.title: Mucosal disease associated with BVDV-1b and BVDV-1e in cattle in Southern Brazil.
papers.abstract: Bovine viral diarrhea virus (BVDV) is an important pathogen of the global cattle industry. Fetal infection during the period of immunotolerance may result in the birth of persistently infected (PI) animals. In such animals, the emergence of or superinfection with cytopathic variants may trigger mucosal disease (MD). The objective of this study was to characterize the anatomopathological and virological aspects of two cases of MD. Animal 1, a 24-month-old presented with diarrhea, weight loss, lameness, sialorrhea, and oral and cutaneous lesions. Animal 2, a four-month-old, exhibited weight loss, intermittent diarrhea, and dehydration. Both animals were submitted to necropsy, and tissue samples from all organs were collected for histopathological evaluation. For BVDV detection, serum samples were subjected to RT-PCR and amplified products were submitted to Sanger sequencing and phylogenetic analysis. Liver and spleen fragments were used for viral isolation in MDBK cell cultures. Immunohistochemistry using the panpestiviral monoclonal antibody 15C5 was performed to detect BVDV antigen. Anatomopathological examination of Animal 1 revealed ulcerative glossitis, erosive stomatitis, erosive and ulcerative esophagitis as well as erosive and ulcerative rumenitis, erosive abomasitis, and ulcerative and crusting dermatitis affecting the nasal planum and the distal limb region. In Animal 2, ulcerative rumenitis, erosive abomasitis, and lymphoid depletion in the ileal Peyer's patches were observed. Both animals were positive for BVDV in immunohistochemistry and classified as BVDV-1e and BVDV-1b based on phylogenetic analysis. Viral isolates from both cases induced cytopathic effect between 48 and 96 h post-inoculation. This study demonstrates distinct lesion patterns in unrelated cases of MD associated with BVDV-1e and BVDV-1b in cattle, constitutes the first report of typical MD associated with these subgenotypes in Brazil.

papers.title: Cordyceps as a multitarget therapeutic platform: biology, bioactive metabolites, and translational challenges.
papers.abstract: Cordyceps-related fungi have garnered global attention as multifunctional therapeutic resources owing to their exclusive entomopathogenic biology, remarkable metabolic diversity, and expanding pharmaceutical bearing. Recent taxonomic revisions determined by molecular phylogenetics have redefined the traditional notion of Cordyceps, revealing distinct evolutionary lineages with species-specific metabolite profiles and biological functions. This review provides a complete and evidence-based synthesis of the taxonomy, ecology, host interactions, chemical composition, biosynthetic pathways, pharmacological activities, and translational prospects of chief medicinal species, including Ophiocordyceps sinensis, Cordyceps militaris, Cordyceps cicadae, and related taxa. Particular emphasis is placed on cordycepin, the signature bioactive nucleoside, and its integration with broader metabolite networks encompassing polysaccharides, sterols, peptides, and secondary metabolites. Current evidence demonstrates that Cordyceps-derived compounds influence multiple interconnected signaling pathways, including AMPK, PI3K/Akt/mTOR, NF-κB, MAPK, and oxidative stress-response networks, thereby contributing to immunomodulatory, anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, anticancer, neuroprotective, and metabolic regulatory effects. The review further reviews recent advances in genomics, transcriptomics, metabolomics, biosynthetic gene-cluster analysis, synthetic biology, metabolic engineering, and exactness fermentation technologies that are redesigning Cordyceps research and industrial production. Critical challenges including species authentication, chemical standardization, pharmacokinetic limitations, product reproducibility, safety evaluation, regulatory requirements, and inadequate clinical validation are also discussed. By integrating biological identity, metabolite biosynthesis, molecular mechanisms, and technological innovation within a translational framework, this review positions Cordyceps as a promising systems-level platform for future therapeutics, functional foods, and precision mycotherapy.

papers.title: CRISPR/Cas13a-Based Nucleic Acid-Functionalized Discrete Floating-Gate Field-Effect Transistor for Amplification-Free Rapid Nipah Virus Detection.
papers.abstract: Nipah virus (NiV) is a highly lethal zoonotic pathogen, and existing rapid diagnostic tools are scarce and reliant on nucleic acid amplification. In this study, we designed and fabricated a thin-film field-effect transistor with an IGZO channel and, for the first time, combined a discrete AuNP floating gate with the CRISPR/Cas13a system to achieve amplification-free detection of NiV. A pair of partially complementary nucleic acid reporter probes was used to attach AuNPs onto the channel, forming a nucleic acid-functionalized discrete floating gate. Under positive gate voltage, the AuNPs electrostatically induce mirror charges in the IGZO channel, amplifying the sensing signal. Additionally, the electrons can be injected from AuNPs into the channel via the Fowler-Nordheim tunneling effect under negative gate voltage, as a potential complementary sensing mechanism. The AuNPs are immobilized via nucleic acid strands, ensuring good biocompatibility. CrRNA was designed and the CRISPR system was optimized for compatibility with the FET, achieving amplification-free detection of NiV standards down to 10° copies/μL within 10 min. This study not only provides a reliable and rapid detection tool for NiV but also establishes a biosensing framework applicable to other pathogens.

papers.title: Fluorescence Turn-On Sensor for Gingipains: Selective Detection of Porphyromonas gingivalis in Periodontal Disease.
papers.abstract: Porphyromonas gingivalis (P.g.), a key pathogen in periodontal disease, plays a critical role in bacterial invasion and is increasingly implicated in systemic conditions, including cardiovascular and neurodegenerative diseases. Its major virulence factors, gingipains, are cysteine proteases essential for pathogenicity. In this study, we introduce Gingitracker, an activity-based fluorescence turn-on sensor for the selective detection of gingipains. Upon covalent binding to the cysteine residue in the active sites of gingipains, Gingitracker undergoes a planar conformational change via the restriction of intramolecular rotation, leading to a significant increase in fluorescence (ΦKgp = 0.54, ΦRgpB = 0.35). In contrast, interactions with control proteases such as mammalian calpain (ΦCalpain = 0.04) and trypsin (ΦTrypsin = 0.03) result in negligible fluorescence, demonstrating Gingitracker's high specificity for gingipains. Gingitracker effectively detects active gingipains in dental plaque samples from periodontitis patients, showing strong correlations with anti-gingipain signals across independent samples (r = 0.73-0.83). These results establish Gingitracker as a sensitive activity-based tool for detecting active gingipains in bacterial and clinical periodontal samples.

papers.title: MouseGPT: A Large-scale Vision-Language Model for Mouse Behavior Analysis
papers.abstract: Analyzing animal behavior is crucial in neuroscience, yet deciphering its intricate dynamics remains challenging. Traditional machine vision approaches detect spontaneous behaviors but are constrained by limited interpretability and reliance on manual labeling, restricting exploration of the full behavioral spectrum. Here, we introduce MouseGPT, an integrated vision-language model and analytical framework that translates raw video of animal activity into natural language to automate open-vocabulary behavior analysis. Built upon a comprehensive dataset of over 42 million frames spanning diverse psychiatric conditions, MouseGPT maps multi-view or single-camera recordings directly into computable semantic representations. An agentic framework leverages these representations for detailed behavior profiling, cross-view stable clustering, and zero-shot novel behavior discovery without requiring labor-intensive annotation. Surpassing conventional kinematics-based pipelines and generalist vision-language models in behavioral precision and adaptability, MouseGPT establishes continuous semantic representations as a powerful tool for deciphering complex ethological dynamics in animal models.

papers.title: RiboDFM: Robust RNA sequence design using backbone-conditioned discrete flow matching
papers.abstract: Designing RNA sequences that fold into predefined 3D structures is central to RNA engineering, yet it remains challenging due to the scarcity of experimentally determined structures and the complex sequence-structure relationships. Here, we present RiboDFM, a backbone-conditioned discrete flow-matching framework for RNA sequence design. RiboDFM progressively resolves fully masked sequences by integrating a geometric backbone encoder, an auxiliary base-pairing prediction head, and language model representations into a discrete flow sampler. To expand our training data, we supplemented experimental structures with a large-scale collection of trRosettaRNA2-predicted models. Across diverse benchmarks, RiboDFM achieves high sequence recovery and generates sequences with greater tertiary-structure self-consistency than existing methods. RiboDFM also performs strongly on aptamer-focused design tasks. Finally, beyond sequence generation, the nucleotide probabilities derived from RiboDFM' s flow trajectory serve as an intrinsic measure of sequence-structure compatibility. This enables reliable confidence estimation for designed sequences, as well as reference-free, zero-shot assessment of predicted structure models. Together, these results establish RiboDFM as an effective framework for structure-based RNA sequence design.

papers.title: Automated Knowledge Graph Construction for CAR T Cell Receptor Design via Hybrid Text Mining
papers.abstract: Designing next-generation Chimeric Antigen Receptors (CARs) requires a systematic understanding of intracellular signaling domains and their downstream biological effects, yet no comprehensive knowledge resource currently exists for this purpose. Here, we present an automated workflow that integrates multiple natural language processing and large language model tools to extract biomolecular interactions from PubMed literature and assemble them into a CAR T cell signaling knowledge graph. Our pipeline combines REACH, INDRA, and Llama 3 across 15 targeted search queries, yielding a directed multi-relational graph of ~7,500 unique interactions among ~1,800 entities, including proteins, biological processes, and chemicals. We further demonstrate that queries incorporating biological process ontology terms retrieve more interaction-rich papers than protein-name-only searches, offering practical guidance for future literature mining efforts. The resulting knowledge base provides a structured foundation for predicting T cell phenotypes and prioritizing intracellular domain candidates for CAR design, with broader applicability to knowledge-driven inference in immunotherapy research.

papers.title: VIOLIN: A modular framework for scalable reconciliation of heterogeneous interaction graphs
papers.abstract: Automated extraction of molecular interactions from scientific literature has outpaced the development of systematic methods for integrating this information with curated models and knowledge graphs. Here we present VIOLIN (Versatile Interaction Organizing to Leverage Information in Networks), a configurable, attribute-aware reconciliation framework that formally compares newly extracted interaction lists against structured baseline graphs. VIOLIN classifies each interaction as a corroboration, contradiction, flagged case, or extension, and supports configurable attribute inclusion strategies and mismatch semantics to adjust reconciliation strictness. We evaluate VIOLIN using interaction lists generated by two traditional NLP systems (REACH, INDRA) and two large language models (GPT-4.1, Llama 3) across multiple literature corpora and structurally distinct baseline graphs. Across all conditions, reconciliation outcomes were stable and interpretable, with extensions dominating and corroboration-contradiction balance reflecting intrinsic structural relationships between baseline graphs and extracted evidence. Sensitivity analyses demonstrate that attribute inclusion and classification scheme selection shift category boundaries predictably. Benchmark evaluations confirm high algorithmic correctness and alignment with expert curation. VIOLIN is publicly available as a Python package and through web-based interface (https://nmzlab.github.io/Tools-UI).

papers.title: An open-source, 3D-printable droplet microfluidics platform with strobe-enhanced microscopy
papers.abstract: Droplet microfluidics underpins many single-cell, precision biomedical, and nanomaterial techniques. However, implementing these methods reproducibly remains challenging outside specialised laboratories due to high equipment costs, operational inflexibility, mechanical impracticality at the microscope stage, as well as open-source pumping solutions that are inadequately validated for low-flow stability. We present an accessible, research-grade, open-source droplet microfluidics platform integrating a compact, microfluidics-optimised microscopy stage with networked syringe-pump control. Designed for local digital fabrication, primarily 3D printing, and widely available components, the platform supports reproducible builds across diverse settings. This setup enables stable droplet generation, observation of rapid droplet dynamics, and automation-ready networked workflows. The microscopy module uses a Raspberry Pi camera and microsecond stroboscopic illumination to capture sharp images of fast-moving droplets without the need for a high-speed camera. A modular hardware interface and extensible, web-accessible software stack provide a path to integrate additional modules and laboratory automation beyond the configuration evaluated here. For infusion, we introduce an open-source syringe pump optimised for low reliable flow rather than maximum rates, combining gearbox-assisted stepper mechanics with workflow-centric control that enables manual intervention (keypad control) and remote operation (web interface and automation hooks). We benchmark droplet regimes, size tuning, and time-stability under low-flow conditions (between 25 and 2500 uL/h) relevant to advanced assays and demonstrate biomedical readiness through the encapsulation and incubation of cells, beads, and bacteria in monodisperse droplets. The platform has been replicated across laboratories in Latin America and globally, including independent builds, supporting reproducibility. All design files, firmware/software, analysis notebooks, and benchmark datasets are openly released.

papers.title: Exome-based Preconception Carrier Screening for the Mexican Jewish Community; Yields and Implications
papers.abstract: Introduction: Preconception carrier screening (PCS) reduces monogenic disease incidence, exemplified by a 90% decline in Tay-Sachs among Ashkenazi populations. The Mexican Jewish Community (MJC), an endogamous population, may have increased prevalence of population-specific genetic disorders. The added value of exome sequencing (ES) over standard panels remains unclear. Objectives: To identify pathogenic/likely pathogenic (P/LP) variants in autosomal recessive (AR), X-linked (XL), and mitochondrial genes, evaluate secondary findings (SF), and define population-specific allele frequencies in the MJC. Methods: From 2020-2025, 787 couples (1,574 individuals) underwent ES following counseling and consent. Genetic data was analyzed including SNVs, CNVs, and mitochondrial DNA. Reporting was limited to P/LP variants and SF. Results: Shared AR carrier status was identified in 49 couples (6.2%): 18.4% associated with severe, 16.3% moderate, and 65.3% with mild conditions. In 71.4% of couples, both partners carried the same variant, consistent with endogamy within the cohort. Maternal findings were identified in 10 women (1.27%). Clinically actionable SF were found in 2.85% of individuals. ES identified 12 at-risk couples (24.4%), undetected by standard panels. Individual genomic profiling revealed 920 rare P/LP variants, including 146 novel alleles, underscoring the distinct genetic architecture of the MJC. Conclusion: ES-based PCS improves detection of at-risk couples beyond conventional screening and supports its use in endogamous populations.

papers.title: Identifying cohorts at elevated risk of cancers using generative modeling of patient health states
papers.abstract: While large language models are powerful generators of new text, forecasting disease progression from longitudinal health histories remains a challenging problem. We introduce GenEHR, an autoregressive generative model trained on electronic health records (EHRs) from millions of patients in diverse health systems. The model learns from real-world multimodal patient histories, including diagnoses, medications, lab values, and procedures while explicitly representing irregular intervals between visits to forecast future clinical events. We combine the general-purpose patient representation learned during foundational training with parameter-efficient supervised adaptation for the task of risk stratification for 17 cancer types. In five large EHR cohorts, supervised adaptation substantially improved prediction performance of a first cancer diagnosis within a five year horizon window. Our retrospective results support the prospective evaluation of GenEHR-CancerRisk as a clinical decision-support tool for prioritizing high-risk patients for screening and prevention of aggressive cancer types, such as pancreatic and ovarian cancer.

papers.title: Predicting the impact of primaquine on Plasmodium falciparum transmission using multiscale modelling
papers.abstract: Primaquine is currently the only widely available antimalarial drug that targets mature \emph{Plasmodium falciparum} gametocytes, the life stage in the human bloodstream that mediates transmission from humans to mosquitoes. The only study that provided large-scale field data suitable for examining the additional impact of the WHO-recommended dose of 0.25 mg/kg primaquine in an artemisinin-based combination therapy (ACT)-based mass drug administration (MDA) campaign was reported by Deng et al. (2018, Clinical Infectious Diseases). The study showed that both ACT alone and ACT plus primaquine substantially reduced average monthly malaria hospital rates and the prevalence of infection after the MDA campaign but no additional benefit was observed with primaquine. These findings challenge our expectations for the population-level impacts of primaquine and are in stark contrast to the predictions (of substantial population-level impacts) made by existing epidemiological-scale modelling studies. To address these knowledge gaps, we hypothesised that individuals' adherence patterns to multi-round MDA campaigns could be a factor that explains these conflicting empirical observations. To examine this hypothesis, we developed a data-driven multiscale agent-based model of malaria infection and transmission, which quantitatively captures both the detailed biology of human infection kinetics and the pharmacodynamic actions of antimalarial drugs. Our model provides a coherent explanation for these apparently disparate observations, including the individual-level gametocytocidal effect of primaquine, the population-level impacts of primaquine in MDA campaigns, and the population-level impacts predicted by previous modelling studies. All three observations can be explained by underlying adherence patterns within a single modelling framework. We used our model to predict the effect of primaquine in routine case management outside MDA, finding that administration could significantly reduce the prevalence of infection, supporting its use as a transmission-blocking intervention against malaria.

papers.title: Functional analysis of NANOS protein variants identified in men with infertility employing zebrafish embryos
papers.abstract: Study question: Are vertebrate NANOS proteins associated with human fertility, and can a rapid in vivo assay in zebrafish be established to evaluate the biological activity of human NANOS variants? Summary answer: Combining a rapid in vivo assay we developed for Nanos protein activity and patient-derived genetic data, we identified NANOS variants that could contribute to male infertility. What is known already: Male infertility affects approximately 17% of the population, but linking specific gene variants to this condition remains challenging. NANOS proteins are essential regulators of germ cell development in different model organisms; however, a rapid and robust in vivo assay for evaluating their activity in the context of human male infertility is currently lacking. Study design, size, duration: Exome/genome data from 3,338 men included in the Male Reproductive Genomics (MERGE) cohort were examined in this study. Of these, 2038 men showed severely impaired spermatogenesis but were otherwise healthy. Ninety-Six men with intact spermatogenesis were included in the study as controls. Additionally, the study included a targeted analysis of NANOS variants in 44 patients from the IMIGC cohort. Participants/materials, setting, methods: The exome/genome data were screened for rare, stop-gain, frameshift, splice site, as well as missense variants in NANOS1, NANOS2, and NANOS3. Human amino acid substitutions were introduced at the corresponding positions in the zebrafish proteins. Ectopic co-expression of wild-type Dnd1 and Nanos3 in zebrafish embryos induces a germ cell-like fate in somatic cells, resulting in severe developmental defects and embryonic lethality. Based on this principle, we established a rapid in vivo assay in which wild-type Dnd1 was co-expressed with wild-type or variant Nanos2 and Nanos3 proteins in live zebrafish embryos, expecting early embryonic death if a variant protein is functional. This assay was used to evaluate the activity of NANOS2 and NANOS3 variants identified in men with infertility. Main results and the role of chance: In human exome/genome sequencing data, we identified one heterozygous missense variant in NANOS2 and two heterozygous missense variants in NANOS3. The function of the variants was examined in the zebrafish using the in vivo assay we developed. Co-expression of wild-type Dnd1 with selected Nanos2 or Nanos3 variants identified in infertile men resulted in defects in induction of the germ cell-like phenotype, demonstrating the power of the biological readout for evaluating the potential effects of patient-derived variants on NANOS protein activity. Together, our analysis enabled the evaluation of single nucleotide variants, whose impact on protein function is difficult to predict, and allowed us to distinguish variants with little or no effect on protein function from those that strongly reduce activity and may potentially contribute to infertility. Limitations, reasons for caution: The assay requires access to zebrafish embryos and basic imaging equipment. Although the functional conservation of NANOS proteins between zebrafish and humans is supported by previous studies, species-specific differences may influence protein activity. Therefore, the zebrafish assay should be considered one component of a broader framework for evaluating NANOS variants as contributing factor for infertility. Wider implications of the findings: Using NANOS2 and NANOS3 as examples, we demonstrate that integrating clinical genetic data with functional cell and developmental biology can help establish links between candidate disease genes and human fertility. This strategy may apply to other germline-specific genes whose ectopic expression produces measurable developmental phenotypes in zebrafish embryos.
